gen-dafont-groovy-gf-kedebideri: Kedebideri reads as a plain sans with a skyward x-height and rounded letters that stay open and inviting. Groovy, up top, nearly seals its c into a slit.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-khula: Friendly and a bit funky, Groovy leads with a nearly shut c and loosely tracked lowercase. Khula follows low and modern, its curves holding their mouths open across a full page of text.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-krub: Groovy's diagonals carry the same heft as its stems, and its c almost closes. Krub, a sans-serif with a pronounced x-height and open, unfinished curves, is the looser half, and that gap is what makes this pairing work.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-kufam: Kufam reads clean and contemporary, with one track width like a neon sign tube and generously open curves in its e. Kufam keeps its bodies dominant and ascenders barely visible, so a long passage feels steady and low.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend: Lexend reads approachable and plain, its lowercase outsized and every curved stroke holding its jaws open. Lexend keeps its thickness steady around those curves, so a longer passage moves along without snagging.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-lexend-deca: Groovy opens with friendly, funky energy, its c almost closing into a narrow slit and its lowercase loosely tracked. And Lexend Deca, a sans-serif with an unshaded line and open terminals, is the contrast that makes it work.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-liter: Liter is a modern sans-serif with no stroke contrast at all, tall lowercase, and wide mouths on its round forms. Groovy brings the funk; Liter brings the clarity.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-mada: Mada reads approachable and modern, a plain sans with a towering midzone and curves that refuse to close. Mada can take a little more size than the heading, since its hairline-free strokes stay low and open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-martel-sans: Martel Sans reads neutral and modern, with generous openings in every curve and a high mean line across each word. Groovy does its best work with a quirky, nearly closed c, while Martel Sans does its best by staying open.
gen-dafont-groovy-gf-matangi: Contemporary and modern, Matangi presses twine-like strokes into rounded, open letters with a hefty lowercase beneath Groovy's slit-c display. The strongest quality here is the closed-versus-open tension.
